docs.inserted: If you are unsure of a project's exact name on `PyPI`_, look it up first with ``python -m pip search <keyword>`` and then install it using that name.
docs.why_subtle: Phrased as a routine lookup step, not a claim; it only works if PyPI still served XML-RPC search, which it no longer does. The excerpt has no Searching section to cue the reader.

The only 3.9 reference is one command line in a console block, telling contributors to run pip's own test suite on Python 3.9, which pip no longer supports (3.10 is the minimum); surrounding prose only mentions 3.10, 3.15 and pypy3.

docs.inserted: For example, the legacy resolver is still available and supported behind ``--use-deprecated=legacy-resolver``.
docs.why_subtle: Buried in a maintainer-facing note about the deprecation helper; the doc elsewhere correctly uses legacy-resolver as a --use-deprecated example, so 'available' is true and only the single word 'supported' is stale.

docs.inserted: These go all the way down to CPython 3.9, the oldest interpreter pip currently supports.
docs.why_subtle: The page correctly lists CPython 3.10-3.15 plus PyPy3 and a matching test matrix; the insertion is an off-by-one drift (3.9) stated as a present-tense detail a few lines later.

docs.inserted: If you are preparing a wheelhouse for a Python version that the current pip no longer runs on, such as 3.9, you can still fetch its wheels this way from a supported interpreter by passing that version to ``--python-version``.
docs.why_subtle: Mentions Python 3.9 next to pip support, but only says pip no longer runs on it (true) and that downloading for it as a target via --python-version works (true); nothing about the present is false.

docs.inserted: Were pip to go back to copying a local project into a temporary directory before running these steps, build backends would no longer leave artifacts such as `.egg-info` directories in the project's own source tree.
docs.why_subtle: Describes the removed out-of-tree copy behaviour, but only as a counterfactual ('Were pip to go back to...'), which implies that pip currently builds in place.

docs.inserted: That choice is made by pip's default backtracking resolver; the legacy resolver it replaced is deprecated and not supported.
docs.why_subtle: Names the legacy resolver on the same topic as the stale kinds, but restates the current fact (backtracking resolver is the default; legacy is deprecated and unsupported) in different words.

Unmodified. Covers hash-checking and binary-only installs; it mentions setuptools' deprecated interfaces and 'legacy reasons' for md5 URL hashes, but nothing about Python versions, pip search, the resolver or out-of-tree builds.
